title: VPC partition simulation, egress quarantine, and graceful-degradation acceptance criteria
creator: Sana Iyer
description: Summary: This ticket defines the requirements and acceptance criteria for a VPC-level partition simulation and an egress-quarantine mode for Redwood Private deployments. The goal is to provide a prescriptive, testable specification that ensures the product can detect and gracefully degrade during partial network partitions and planned maintenance that limits outbound connectivity. This covers: 1) controlled partial partition tests (simulated packet loss / route blackholes) against critical control-plane and artifact endpoints; 2) an 'egress quarantine' operating mode where runtime continues serving from cached artifacts and read-only capabilities while blocking non-essential outbound calls; 3) automated rollback and observable criteria for fail-safe recovery; and 4) end-to-end test harness and runbook for customers and SREs.
scope_clarification: In scope: controlled simulation tooling and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments affecting networking and upgrade flows. Out of scope: major cloud provider networking automation (we'll provide tests and guidance, not vendor-specific plugins) and changes to customer IAM systems. This ticket does not implement the quarantine feature UI; it defines API contracts, runtime behavior, observability signals, and automated test plans.
background: Customers operating in highly regulated environments require guarantees that: (a) upgrades or transient network failures do not lead to silent data loss or unexpected secrets leakage; (b) the runtime can continue serving critical traffic using cached artifacts (models, tokenizers, keys in KMS-proxied mode) when egress is intentionally restricted; and (c) the operator can simulate realistic partition scenarios pre-deployment to validate outage SLOs. Current tests validate full offline upgrades and zero-egress baseline but do not cover partial partitions or graduated degradation modes. This work closes that gap.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Partition simulation harness exists and can emulate at least three failure modes: control-plane blackhole (no API reachability to control-plane endpoints), partial egress loss (only specific external endpoints blocked), and asymmetric routing (one direction blocked). The harness must be runnable from customer VPC test instances and from our staging clusters.

AC-2: Runtime behavior under egress quarantine: when the quarantine flag is enabled or ports to artifact registry are blocked, the runtime must continue serving using local model artifacts and KV cache for at least 6 hours, and must not attempt to leak keys or plaintext artifacts outside VPC boundaries. Any attempt to download new models must be rejected with a clear telemetry event.

AC-3: Observable signals: Console and metrics must surface a distinct 'egress.quarantine' state, with accompanying traces showing blocked outbound attempts (HTTP 0 / TCP RST) and a per-token SLO degradation estimate. Alerts must fire for: loss of control-plane heartbeat > 30s, cache hit ratio < 60% under quarantine, and model mismatch checks during an upgrade attempt.

AC-4: Upgrade safety gating: The upgrade orchestration must detect partitioned nodes and automatically defer node-level upgrades if the partition reduces the reachable capacity below the configured safety threshold (default 70% of reserved capacity). A canary upgrade must not progress to full rollout during an active quarantine or unresolved partition.

AC-5: Rollback triggers and automated recovery: The system must define deterministic rollback triggers including: error rates > 5% for 2 minutes, token latency p95 regressions > 250ms above baseline for 2 minutes, or loss of control-plane quorum for > 60s. When a trigger fires during a rollout, automated rollback must initiate and emit a post-mortem template into the incident log.

AC-6: Test-driven verification: The delivery includes an automated test suite (integration tests + chaos scenarios) that runs in CI. Tests must validate that quarantine mode blocks outbound artifact pulls, that cached-serving keeps serving inference requests (functional correctness on a curated prompt set), and that the observability signals defined in AC-3 are produced.

AC-7: Customer runbook and remediation steps: A concise runbook must be provided covering: how to enable quarantine, how to run the partition simulator, required dashboards to inspect, how to trigger a safe rollback, and recommended communication templates for customers during maintenance windows.

AC-8: Security and KMS constraints: When running under quarantine or partitioned conditions, KMS operations must not send key material outside the VPC. If KMS is operated in remote mode and is unreachable, the runtime must reject operations requiring new plaintext key material and surface a clear error (no silent fallback to local keys).

AC-9: Minimal customer impact measured: With quarantine enabled, at least 90% of 99th-percentile customer queries that depend only on cached models must succeed (functional pass/fail) during a 1-hour simulated egress block in staging. Non-cached flows may return explicit retryable errors.

AC-10: Documentation and APIs: API contract for quarantine mode and partition simulation CLI must be documented in the Private Deployments guide with examples, and the CLI must return structured exit codes for automation consumption.
test_plan: 1) Add partition-sim tests to infra-ci: run simulated blackhole and partial egress scenarios against a dedicated staging Private cluster. 2) Run quarantine-mode functional tests against curated prompt set (10 prompts across chat/generation/embeddings). 3) Execute upgrade-canary under simulated partition and verify gating logic. 4) Validate observability by asserting presence of 'egress.quarantine' metric and corresponding trace spans. 5) Security review verifies KMS behavior under partition.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal staging only (ops + SRE), run full test harness. Phase 2: invite 3 pilot customers on Dedicated capacity with opt-in quarantine simulation during a scheduled maintenance window. Phase 3: GA to Private customers with documentation and SDK flags. Rollout controlled via a feature flag with immediate kill-switch.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives in partition detection could block legitimate upgrades -> Mitigation: require 2 independent signals (control-plane heartbeat + cache hit ratio) before gating.

Risk: Quarantine could reduce revenue-bearing requests -> Mitigation: quarantine is opt-in for pilot customers and is accompanied by conservative capacity thresholds and clear customer-facing messaging.
Risk: KMS unavailable causes all write operations to fail -> Mitigation: document which operations are writable vs read-only under quarantine and provide a graceful error surface to integrators.
Risk: Test harness may not reflect customer network topologies -> Mitigation: provide customers with runnable containerized simulator and reproducible scripts to run in their VPCs.
Risk: Observability noise from simulated failures -> Mitigation: tag simulation runs and provide filters in dashboards so SREs can exclude them from production alerts.

Risk: Legal/regulatory concerns about running network simulation in customer VPCs -> Mitigation: require explicit customer opt-in, narrow scope tests, and pre-coordination with customer security teams.

Risk: Rolling upgrades during partitions could trigger split-brain -> Mitigation: design orchestration to prefer read-only serving and to avoid write-path configuration changes during suspected partitions.
Risk: Time drift causes false quorum decisions -> Mitigation: ensure NTP sync checks before test execution and surface time drift metrics.
Risk: Artifact consistency across nodes when serving from cache -> Mitigation: add periodic artifact checksum gossip and fail fast on mismatch.
notes:
- Aligns with existing zero-egress and offline-upgrade work but focuses on graduated degradation and testability.
- Cross-team: requires engine changes to emit quarantine telemetry, infra changes for simulation hooks, and docs + sales collateral for pilot customers.
- Meet upstream: schedule architecture walkthrough with Engine (ENG), Infra (ENG), and Security next week.
